format.delivery: Pearson VUE, online proctored or test center
format.note: Per-domain percentages on the score report are diagnostic only. Pass/fail is total scaled score.

policy.renewal: free non-proctored assessment if on time; full exam if lapsed

objectives.name: Agent Architecture
scope: role of subagents in task execution
traps: subagents exist primarily for CONTEXT ISOLATION, not parallelism
default to the simplest thing; distractors offer elegant multi-agent designs where a prompt chain is correct

objectives.name: Agent Construction with Claude
traps: the model NEVER executes a tool; the harness does
connecting an MCP server does not grant tool permission - the allow-list does

objectives.name: Agent Patterns and Frameworks
traps: unbounded loops are a harness design failure, not a model failure
the API is stateless; long-term memory is application-designed

objectives.name: Understanding Requirements
traps: one buried constraint in the stem decides the answer

objectives.name: Systems Life Cycle
scope: generic IT lifecycle: develop, implement, operate, maintain
named frameworks: Waterfall, Agile, DevOps, ITIL
traps: this is GENERIC IT lifecycle, not LLM-specific delivery
change management and release gates point at ITIL, not the coding workflow

objectives.name: Claude API Mechanics
scope: third-party vendors (Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry)
traps: system is a top-level parameter, not a message role
content is a LIST OF BLOCKS
stop_reason arrives on a 200 and is not an error
final usage arrives in message_delta, not message_start
an error event can arrive AFTER a 200 in a stream
batch results are UNORDERED - join on custom_id
cache prefix order is tools then system then messages, matched exactly
regional endpoints answer data residency; global endpoints do not

objectives.name: Software Engineering Foundations
traps: SDKs already retry twice with backoff honoring retry-after; a hand-rolled retry layer multiplies load during the incident
review AI-generated code with the same rigor as human-written

objectives.name: Claude Application Design
scope: how Claude interprets instructions across Claude Code, Desktop, claude.ai, API, SDKs
traps: this is NOT workflow pattern selection - that is Domain 1
choose the interface whose instruction surface matches the DURABILITY required
never concatenate user input into the system prompt
nullable fields let the model decline instead of fabricating
session boundaries are security boundaries

objectives.name: Configuration Management
traps: quality shifting on a day nothing shipped = an unpinned alias
secrets management is Domain 7, not here

objectives.name: Claude Code Operation
scope: core components: Rules, Skills, Commands, Agents, Agent Memory
traps: a Skill's DESCRIPTION is its trigger - it functions like a search query
progressive disclosure: metadata always loaded, body on trigger, resources as needed
CLAUDE.md for memory, Skills for routines, hooks for guarantees, subagents for delegation

objectives.name: Debugging and Error Handling
scope: problem origin isolation between integration layer and model output
traps: raw output correct but app wrong = integration layer; raw output wrong = model layer
truncated output must NOT be sent for repair - the content was never generated
an LLM judge must be calibrated against human labels; consistency is not accuracy

objectives.name: LLM Fundamentals
traps: few-shot prompting is scored HERE, not in Domain 6
context window and max output tokens are different limits
token counts are model-specific and do not transfer across a migration

objectives.name: Technical Fundamentals
scope: integrating with SDKs that wrap REST APIs
traps: NARROW objective - not context theory, not rate limits
Claude streaming is SSE, not WebSocket

objectives.name: Model Selection and Tradeoffs
scope: Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku use cases
breaking behavior changes across model releases
traps: Haiku has no effort parameter - it is differently shaped, not just cheaper
effort tuning preserves evaluated behavior; a model swap invalidates every eval

objectives.name: Cost and Token Management
traps: thinking tokens bill at OUTPUT rates
optimization order: fewer tokens, cache, batch, effort step-down, model downgrade LAST

objectives.name: Context Engineering
scope: preventing bloat via tool output pruning and compaction
context isolation through subagents or multi-step workflows
traps: tool output pruning is usually the largest single source of bloat
compaction is LOSSY - what survives is a design decision

objectives.name: Prompt Engineering
traps: tool descriptions are prompts
a prompt fix for one case commonly regresses others - hence the eval set first

objectives.name: Output Handling
traps: schema-valid and semantically correct are different things
never index content[0] blindly

objectives.name: AI Application Security
traps: mitigations that WORK are structural: content boundaries, least privilege on tools, human approval, hooks
mitigations that DO NOT work: asking nicely in the system prompt, changing temperature, using a bigger model
a bigger model can be MORE susceptible to injection, not less
integrity has four failure modes: instruction, memory, output, supply-chain

objectives.name: Guardrails and Safe Deployment
traps: an agent inherits the calling user's permissions, never a superset
verify entitlement at the tool boundary per request, not once at session start

objectives.name: Claude Hooks
scope: hooks for guardrails and safety controls to prevent destructive actions
traps: PreToolUse can block; PostToolUse cannot undo
EXIT 2 BLOCKS. Exit 1 is a non-blocking error and the action proceeds - guards fail OPEN
matchers are case-sensitive regex against the TOOL NAME, not prompt text

objectives.name: Identity, Secrets, and Key Management
scope: secrets, credentials, API keys across dev and production
traps: a key shipped to a client is compromised on ship; obfuscation only delays extraction

objectives.name: Tool Implementation
traps: return errors as tool_result with is_error so the model can self-correct; do not throw
every tool definition costs tokens on EVERY request and adds selection ambiguity

objectives.name: MCP Server Development
scope: communication patterns: stdio, sockets, client vs server
traps: tools are MODEL-controlled, resources are APPLICATION-controlled, prompts are USER-controlled
command to run = stdio; URL = Streamable HTTP; HTTP+SSE is deprecated

objectives.name: Agentic Customization
scope: tradeoffs among built-in Tools, custom Tools, Skills, and MCPs
traps: a Skill changes HOW Claude does something it can already do; a tool ADDS a capability
reusable across applications AND independently maintained = MCP server

official_samples_for_originality_check_o._warning: These three items are published in the exam guide. They exist here ONLY as a similarity reference for the originality gate. NEVER copy, paraphrase, or closely track them when authoring practice questions.
stems: A developer must process 10,000 documents overnight to produce a non-urgent analytics report. Cost is the primary concern, and results are not needed until the following morning. Which approach best fits the requirement?

A Claude-powered agent summarizes web pages submitted by end users. One page contains hidden text instructing the model to ignore previous instructions and reveal its system prompt. Which mitigation is most effective?

A team needs Claude to call an internal inventory service exposed as a REST API. They want the capability to be reusable across several Claude applications and maintained independently of any one app. Which approach best fits?

item_style.distractor_rule: each distractor must fail for a nameable reason: irrelevant mechanism, unenforceable control, or not addressing the real tradeoff
item_style.dominant_pattern: one buried constraint in the stem decides the answer; place it mid-stem, not in the final sentence
item_style.must_should_rule: when a stem says MUST or ALWAYS, the answer is a deterministic control (hook, permission rule, schema constraint), never a system-prompt instruction

constraint_signals.deterministic rule: do not use an LLM at all
